**Hypothesis (data-grounded, from correlation-matrix PCA on the 12 forms of capital over the 39 hundred-year time slices of capital.csv, BCE 4300→500):**

In the PCA of the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices, the symbolic capital components — house size, daggers, and hatchets/swords — are characterized by **negative values on PC1** and by a **PC2 distribution that is centered near the PC2 axis except for the house-size component, which pulls toward the negative half of PC2**.

On PC1 (~30.3% of the variance), all three symbolic components load **negatively** and behave coherently as a single block on the negative PC1 pole: hatchet/sword has the strongest negative loading (−0.30), followed by dagger (−0.27), then house size (−0.23); accordingly each is negatively correlated with the PC1 slice scores (hatchet/sword r = −0.57, dagger r = −0.51, house size r = −0.43). High symbolic capital therefore corresponds to low (negative) PC1 values.

Across PC2 (~19.5% of the variance), the symbolic components are distributed differently: **daggers and hatchets/swords sit essentially on the PC2 axis** (PC2 loadings ≈ −0.07 and −0.05, respectively, with weak PC2 correlations of −0.11 and −0.08) — PC2 carries almost none of their variance, so they are spread/centered near zero along PC2. **House size is the exception**, carrying the only substantive negative PC2 loading among the three (−0.33) with a strong negative PC2 correlation (r = −0.50), placing house size on the negative half of PC2. Consistent with this, the hundred-year slices with the highest symbolic capital are distributed across both sides of PC2 (7 of 13 top-tercile slices at PC2 < 0, 6 at PC2 > 0), i.e., symbolic capital broadly spans PC2 rather than being confined to one side — the modest negative shift being driven mainly by house size.

In short: symbolic capital (house size, daggers, hatchets/swords) is a uniformly negative contribution to PC1, while on PC2 daggers and hatchets/swords cluster around the origin (near zero) and house size is displaced toward negative PC2.

Across PC2, daggers and hatchets/swords sit near the PC2 axis (loadings ~-0.07 and -0.05; weak PC2 correlations), i.e. they are centered near zero on PC2, whereas house size has a substantive negative PC2 loading (-0.33, r=-0.50) placing it on the negative half of PC2. Symbolic capital thus spans PC2 (high-symbolic-capital slices fall on both sides of PC2) with a modest negative shift driven by house size.
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded capital.csv (decimal=','), dropped group/color per metadata, kept the 12 Z-capital columns; verified 39 rows = 100-year slices (BCE 4300->500 step 100, no missing). 2) Cross-checked that all 12 Z series exactly equal the *_inter columns of time_series_data.csv at CE=-BCE (max|diff|=0 over 37 slices). 3) Standardized the 12 columns (correlation-matrix PCA) and ran eigendecomposition (numpy) -> PC1=30.3%, PC2=19.5% of variance. 4) Read off PC1 loadings and PC2 loadings for Zhausgr (House Size), ZDolch (Dagger), ZAxtSchwert (Hatchet/Sword); corroborated PC2 distribution via Pearson r of each component with PC2 slice scores and via the PC2 scores of top-tercile high-symbolic-capital slices. 5) Formulated the natural-language hypothesis from these read-off values.
